scenario: Same as local_agent_outlives, but the host process injects a NEW user message via stdin ~2s after the parent's message_delta stop_reason=end_turn (while the subagent is still running). Confirms that Claude CLI accepts mid-wait stdin cleanly and re-rounds without errors.

stdin_injection.content: What is happening right now in this session? Reply in one short sentence and stop.

cli_re_round_init_after_injection.note: CLI emits system.init within 32ms of the injected message, opening a new round in the same logical turn.

parent_response_to_injection.text: Waiting for the background "sleep-haiku" subagent to finish before continuing.
parent_response_to_injection.note: Parent processed the injected message coherently; original subagent kept running uninterrupted.

first_and_only_result_envelope.note: Only ONE result envelope across the entire 8.9s cascade containing three parent end_turn signals.

implication_for_fix: Empirically safe to unblock the composer / clear the working indicator on parent message_delta stop_reason=end_turn. The CLI handles stdin during the wait window cleanly and re-rounds itself. There is no risk of dropped messages, double-processing, or wire-protocol error from sending input during the gap.
purpose: Back the safety argument for the soft-round-close turn-complete behaviour. Confirms the most-cited UX risk ("composer unblocking might race with task_notification cascade") does not materialize in practice on Claude CLI 2.1.118.
